To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in the absence of ANG II, the physiological effects of ANG II are mediated by ANG III, 2) the physiological effects of the ANG-(1--7) are mediated by ANGs other than ANG-(1,7), and 3) the physiological effects mediated by ANG IV are not mediated by ANG II receptors.

1) the biological effects of ANG II on sodium and water excretion are not mediated by other angiotensin peptides, 2) the biological effects on sodium and water are mediated by the AT1 receptor, and 3), the biological effects of the renin-angiotensin system are not mediated by the effects of angiotensin on aldosterone.

1) the effects of ANG II on renal function are mediated by the classical ANG II receptor and are not mimicked by other angiotensins; and 2) ANGs other than ANG I and ANG II are not involved in the regulation of renal function in the normal human subject.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the octapeptide ANG III and two shorter angiotensin fragments, ANG-(l-7) and the heptapeptide ANG IV, on renal function in humans.
the effects of angiotensins on the kidney.
the role of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) and its components in the regulation of renal function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ANG III and, to a lesser extent, ANG IV may be physiological modulators of renal sodium and potassium handling and aldosterone secretion.
the effects of ANG III are not identical to ANG II and that ANG III is cleared much more rapidly than ANG II.
, in the absence of endogenous ANG II, only ANG II is a potent vasoconstrictor, natriuretic, and kaliuretic peptide, whereas ANG-(1--7), ANG III, and ANG IV have little or no effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ANG II is the most important effector molecule of the renin-angiotensin system.
ANG II is a powerful natriuretic and diuretic peptide, which, however, is counteracted by aldosterone and other factors.
the renin system is not only a system for the regulation of blood pressure but also a system for the control of renal function and electrolyte excretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ANG III is the major angiotensin in human plasma.
the effects of the renin-angiotensin system are not limited to the actions of ANG II, but also include those of ANG III and, possibly, ANG IV and ANG-(1–7).
the biological actions of ANG II, ANG III, and ANG IV differ substantially in the human, and that the effects of ANG III are not mediated via ANG II receptors.
